page: Vultr voc-g-4c-16gb-80s-amd is an instance in the Optimized Cloud Compute family, provisioned with a 1:4 core-to-memory ratio suitable for general-purpose computing. The server is powered by an x86_64 AMD EPYC processor running at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz, providing 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 2 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled. The CPU configuration includes 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of shared L3 cache, with hardware support for vector and cryptographic instruction sets including AVX-512 (F, VNNI, BF16), AES, VAES, and SHA-NI.

System memory consists of 16.0 GB of RAM, backed by an integrated 80 GB NVMe solid-state drive for local storage and one complimentary public IPv4 address. Synthetic benchmarks reveal notable strengths in single-threaded tasks, where the server scores in the top tier for stress-ng single-core compute (3,435.28) and achieves strong performance in single-threaded compression benchmarks (32.1 GB/sec in gzip). Large-block memory write throughput is also solid at 113.87 GB/sec. Conversely, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and PassMark database operations place in the bottom 25%, demonstrating that parallel throughput is constrained by the two physical cores.

The instance delivers consistent dedicated CPU allocation without the risk of noisy-neighbor throttling found in burstable tiers. While static web serving throughput and medium-model LLM inference speeds are modest, the balanced compute, memory, and local NVMe storage deliver efficient resource density for application backends, microservices, continuous integration runners, caching layers like Redis, and mid-sized general workloads.
description: Vultr voc-g-4c-16gb-80s-amd is a general-purpose virtual server within the Optimized Cloud Compute line, configured with 4 dedicated vCPUs from an AMD EPYC processor (2 physical cores at 2.0 GHz) and 16.0 GB of system memory. It includes 80 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and instruction set extensions including AVX-512, VAES, and SHA-NI. The server demonstrates top-tier single-core CPU throughput in stress-ng alongside strong single-threaded compression metrics, though multi-core parallel scaling reflects its physical two-core constraint. With a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, high memory write bandwidth, and dedicated compute resources, this instance provides dependable, cost-efficient infrastructure for continuous integration pipelines, microservices, Redis caching nodes, and general enterprise application hosting.
